correctness.rationale: For all nondegenerate parallelograms K and any P in its closed body, polar integration of rays gives exactly pi M_K(P)=∫_K |x-P|^{-1} dx. A layer-cake identity coupled with Brunn–Minkowski for K=-K yields potential maximal at its center, strictly if P≠center, even on the boundary. A sheared centered parallelogram has horizontal slices of length a centered at sy/h; rearranging every slice toward 0 only increases inverse-distance potential and removes the shear while decreasing perimeter, with strictness unless shear 0. The rectangle potential equals 2[a asinh(h/a)+h asinh(a/h)]. As asinh is strictly concave, weighted Jensen with weights a/(a+h), h/(a+h) and arguments h/a,a/h gives upper p asinh(1), with equality exactly a=h; dividing pi yields the sharp mean chord coefficient. The proof is for uniform orientation of a chord through fixed P, not random affine-line chord sampling. Independent quadrature/identity comparisons passed 20 rectangles; the proof holds for arbitrary real sizes and shear.
residual_risks: An equivalent older square-is-optimal potential inequality might exist in classical integral geometry; inverse distance center maximization itself is known and not claimed new; different random-chord models should not be conflated.
